evidence: Every existing PARCEL_RECORD_SLATE entry has a dedicated *ServeCutover.ts wrapper (or, for the cadRoll six, attachCadRollOverlaysToFacets) that calls resolveAllowlist/resolveAllowlistState for that exact rail key. Repo-wide grep for resolveAllowlist call sites returns exactly the 13 known wrapper files plus parcelRecordAllowlist.ts/parcelGateVerdictRead.ts themselves -- nothing else.

No wrapper exists for parcelAreaSqFt, maxHeightFt, maxLotCoveragePct, or maxFootprintSqFt. Repo-wide grep for these four names outside test files hits only: nodeFacetBakeTier1.ts / nodeFacetBakeTier2.ts (type-only interface fields, never a resolveAllowlist call), buildableEnvelope/derive.ts + geometry.ts + reconcileAtomEnvelope.ts (bake-time geometry, no parcel_record read), and brokerageResearchAreaContext.ts (a downstream text-formatting consumer that only reads whatever facets.envelope already carries -- it does not independently query parcel_record or consult the allowlist).

The shared response-assembly functions (structuralFactToFacetsWire.ts's attachVerdictLayersToFacets and attachCadRollOverlaysToFacets -- the exact functions L1's close says to trace instead of the per-rail wrapper) contain zero references to any of the four rail names.

computeTier1Envelope (nodeFacetBakeTier1.ts:92-122), the program's own named root-cause function, has exactly two return branches and BOTH are status:'declined' -- neither branch ever sets parcelAreaSqFt/maxHeightFt/maxLotCoveragePct/maxFootprintSqFt on its return object, even though they are declared as optional fields on Tier1EnvelopeFacet. So there is also no LEGACY value for these four rails today -- unlike every rail L1 audited (legacy-absent/-unreachable/-reachable), this is a rail where NEITHER path currently exists in this repo's serve layer.

Confirmed setbackRules -- one of S1's five written rails -- has ZERO occurrences anywhere in legacy-design-tools' src tree (repo-wide grep, zero hits). It is not part of SETBACK_RAIL_KEYS (setbacksFactFromParcelRecord.ts's own list is Front/Side/Rear/Corner only, 4 keys, no Rules). step2_criticalFinding_vacuousSlateRisk.contrastWithPrecedent: This file's own established pattern (utilityService/overlayDistricts/agValuation/schoolDistrict) DOES slate rails ahead of their gate verdict landing -- but every one of those precedents already had its wrapper file calling resolveAllowlist at slating time; only the verdict was pending, so an unslated/no-verdict pair fails closed to 'legacy' by construction. parcelAreaSqFt has no wrapper AT ALL, so it is not the same situation: there is no code path that would ever consult its slate membership, verdict-pending or not.
step2_criticalFinding_vacuousSlateRisk.decision_thisCheckpoint: NOT adding parcelAreaSqFt's 4 passing pairs to PARCEL_RECORD_SLATE this checkpoint. Slating them would be textually compliant but functionally inert -- exactly the class of defect ("it runs perfectly, every test passes, and it cannot succeed on any branch") this program's own preamble names as the reason it exists. Building a NEW ServeCutover wrapper (following the established per-rail pattern: injectable test store, resolveAllowlist call, wiring into the response-assembly path, tests) would make it non-vacuous, but that is materially more scope than "add pairs to PARCEL_RECORD_SLATE" as dispatched, is not named in this dispatch's in-scope or out-of-scope lists, and is a scope decision for the planner, not a unilateral in-lane call (DEV_PROCESS 5.4).
